verdict_note: At a4e03d68 nothing found that breaks the build or a test, gives wrong pixels on the frames the lane draws today, causes undefined behaviour or a GPU hang, or breaks a binding decision. These all check out: barriers and layouts; object lifetimes and drop order; the descriptor/binding map against the shader; staging offsets; the checked-in SPIR-V against manifest.json; the spv-build lock subset; the one approved Cargo.lock line; the probe entry and its self-test; the product closure; release builds enabling nothing. Fix first for three reasons. (1) F1: the validation gate does not enforce the lead's READY condition. Warnings are never asserted, and every non-error message without the VALIDATION or PERFORMANCE type is filed as an expected loader warning without a look at its id or text, so a new loader message passes unseen. Both fixes are cheap. (2) F2 and F3 are latent wrong pixels and an unbounded allocation in the public UiPass API; they are small changes in ui.rs. (3) SMB-GUI-FRAME-1 lands before this lane. The rebase conflicts in gui/mod.rs (4 hunks) and README.md (2 hunks), and GUI-FRAME-1's new tests/gui_chrome.rs:535 fails against the lane's CHROME string (F7). The native-host suite must run on the rebased tree anyway. Order: apply F1 to F5, wait for GUI-FRAME-1, rebase (rebase_note), then ONE bundled run on the rebased tip. That saves a second run.

findings.certainty: READ (code); UNVERIFIED (the exact loader message text, which the lane file only paraphrases)
findings.severity: gate gap: the READY condition (validation errors 0 and VUID warnings 0) is not enforced by any test, and a new loader warning is never caught
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-vulkan/src/owner.rs:146-152 (on_validation_message: general_only and not ERROR goes to LOADER_WARNINGS and returns before reading id or text); tests/support/mod.rs:93-100 (assert_validation_clean asserts errors only); crates/hsk-studio-native-host/tests/validation/mod.rs:21-35 (assert_clean asserts errors only, prints warnings); tests/gui_vulkan.rs:155-159 and :300-305 (inline checks, errors only)
findings.what: The type separation works for VUID messages: the layer tags them VALIDATION, so they are counted in `warnings` and their ids land in `first`. Two gaps remain. (a) No test asserts warnings == 0. A validation or performance warning only gets printed, so READY's 'VUID warnings 0' depends on someone reading logs. (b) Any GENERAL-only message below ERROR is counted as a loader warning: from the loader, from a driver or ICD manifest, or from any layer. The callback keeps no id or text for it, so nothing can tell the expected 'layer forced disabled by VK_LOADER_LAYERS_DISABLE' notes from a new one. The count cannot be pinned either: 9 per instance is this machine's implicit-layer count, and the swapchain receipt in captures-346c6aff shows 27, which is three instances in one process.
findings.scenario: A later edit triggers a validation warning, or a driver or layer update adds a loader warning (a manifest or version mismatch, say). Every GPU test stays green, the helpers report the run as clean, and the lane goes READY with the warning in it.
findings.fix: (a) When the state is on, assert v.warnings == 0 in assert_validation_clean, in assert_clean (including the receipt's validation_report.warnings) and in the two inline checks of gui_vulkan.rs. (b) In the callback, count a GENERAL non-error message as a loader warning only when its message_id_name is the loader's and its text matches the forced-disabled note. Count everything else as a warning and keep its id in `first`; the text goes to stderr only, as now. Take the exact text from one observed run: today these messages return before the stderr line, so add a one-off print or read the loader's source string. (c) Test: a GENERAL warning that is not the expected note lands in `warnings`, through a unit test of a factored classification function with no device.

findings.severity: latent wrong pixels: a later draw samples texels that were never uploaded, with no error and no counter
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-vulkan/src/ui.rs:311 and :343-355 (rollback only on Stop::Again, never on Stop::Refused); :236, :678 (ui_pass_limit refusals after entries were placed, and at :627/:672 after a page reset); :1088-1092 (no invalidation when run_pass fails after record); :1199 (ImageTex.bytes set before the submit)
findings.what: The Recorder records residency when it plans, not when an upload runs. (1) When a recording is refused with ui_pass_limit, attempt() returns without removing the entries it placed (new_glyphs, new_icons, icon_bytes). The plan is thrown away, so those uploads never run, but the entries stay Resident. (2) When record succeeds and a later run_pass returns an error that does not poison the submitter, the uploads of that pass and every later pass never ran. Such errors: out_of_memory from Tex::new (:1190) or from staging or instance growth (:1210, :1217); invalid_buffer from write_at; descriptor pool or set errors; invalid_pane from pane_target. On top of that, ImageTex.bytes already holds the new bytes, so the image is never uploaded again. The brief says the atlas holds no authority and any reset gives the same frame; this path breaks that.
findings.scenario: Frame N is a flood and is refused with ui_pass_limit, a 'validation' class refusal, not device loss. Frame N+1 is normal on the same UiPass: glyphs placed in N count as Resident, get no upload, and draw garbage. Today both hosts end the run on any refusal (window.rs:605-609 fail then el.exit; offscreen returns), so studio-vk is not affected. Any caller that keeps a UiPass after a refused frame is.
findings.fix: In UiPass::draw, on any Err from record or run_pass, invalidate everything: reset both atlases, clear icon_bytes, set glyph_fresh and icon_fresh, and clear every ImageTex.bytes (or drop the image textures). In attempt(), apply the Again rollback on Refused as well. Test: a frame refused with ui_pass_limit (small max_passes and a forced glyph page break), then a normal frame, must equal the bytes of a cold draw of that normal frame.

findings.severity: unbounded allocation; brief hostile bound (f) ('every texture is bounded by MAX_PIXELS 64 Mpx') not implemented
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-vulkan/src/ui.rs:480-492 (images checked against maxImageDimension2D and MAX_FRAME_IMAGES only); :1180-1214 (all fresh image bytes of a pass go into one Vec `blob` and one staging HostBuffer); :1141-1153 (buffer() doubles with no cap); :1199 (a full retained copy per image)
findings.what: An image is accepted up to max_image_side per side (16384 on this device, so 1 GiB RGBA), with no check against MAX_PIXELS (refusal.rs:110). Up to 256 images per frame can be fresh in one pass. The Vec blob, the doubling staging buffer and the retained copies then grow without a cap. A failed Vec growth aborts the process, so there is no typed refusal. On the host path today one document image is bounded by rgba_len at gui/mod.rs:410 (64 Mpx). Each document change there costs about 256 MiB of blob, 256 MiB of host-visible staging (kept afterwards), 256 MiB of retained copy and 256 MiB of device memory: bounded, but about 3x the image.
findings.scenario: An API caller or a later panel supplies several large ImageRefs in one frame, or one 16384 x 16384 image. Memory exhaustion aborts the process, or a 1 GiB texture is accepted although it is over MAX_PIXELS.
findings.fix: Skip and count (image_over_limit) any image whose w*h exceeds MAX_PIXELS. Cap the staging bytes per pass at 64 Mpx x 4 = 256 MiB: break the pass, or upload each image in its own waited submit, when the next image would pass the cap. buffer() refuses out_of_memory at its cap instead of doubling. Tests: an image above MAX_PIXELS is counted and not drawn, as the CPU painter's bounds allow; two images whose sum passes the cap still draw at parity.

findings.severity: wrong outcome against the CPU painter: a whole Vulkan frame refused (icon), or page thrash and ui_pass_limit (glyphs), on an entry larger than the page maximum
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-vulkan/src/ui.rs:621-640 (glyph Placed::Full at max: reset, pass break, then counted); :664-679 (icon: reset, pass break, then Err(ui_pass_limit)); atlas.rs:47 (place returns None both for a full page and for an entry larger than the page)
findings.what: The recorder cannot tell 'page full' from 'entry larger than the page'. At the maximum side it resets the whole page and breaks the pass before it finds out the entry can never fit. For a glyph larger than 4096 that throws away every resident glyph and spends a pass; 15 such glyphs in one frame return ui_pass_limit. For an icon mask larger than 2048 it refuses the whole frame (:678), where the CPU painter draws it.
findings.scenario: An Icon prim whose mask is over 2048 px. The mask is requested at px = the smaller side of the snapped rect, so at scale 8 any icon rect over 256 logical px qualifies. After GUI-FRAME-1, a rotated ruler label wider than 2048 px also qualifies, because those labels reach this page as IconMasks (kumihimo-ui Text::rotated_label). --chrome vulkan then exits 3 on a frame the CPU chrome draws.
findings.fix: Before any reset or pass break, if w or h exceeds the atlas maximum side, skip and count it: glyph_refusals for a glyph; missing_resources or a new icon_over_limit for an icon. No reset, no break, no refusal. Test: one oversized glyph and one oversized icon in a frame cause no reset and no extra pass, and the frame draws.

findings.severity: undefined behaviour on devices whose framebuffer or viewport limits are below the pane extent (not reachable on the RTX 3090, whose limits are 32768)
findings.where: crates/hsk-studio-vulkan/src/ui.rs:1346-1348 (renderArea and viewport = pane extent); :918-926 (with_limits reads only maxImageDimension2D)
findings.what: A pane can be up to MAX_EXTENT 16384 per side. draw() renders at that extent without checking maxFramebufferWidth/Height or maxViewportDimensions, whose core minimum is 4096. On a device with smaller limits that is invalid usage, and it returns no typed refusal.
findings.scenario: A Vulkan 1.3 device with an 8192 framebuffer limit and a window or capture above 8192 px with --chrome vulkan.
findings.fix: Record the three limits in UiPass::new and refuse invalid_extent in draw when the pane exceeds them.

lead_questions: Synchronization coverage (UNVERIFIED): VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation's default settings run core checks, not synchronization validation, so 'errors 0' does not prove the barrier chain. My read found no hazard: the pane UNDEFINED or TRANSFER_SRC to COLOR_ATTACHMENT barrier after the presenter's blit on the same queue; the COLOR_ATTACHMENT to TRANSFER_SRC barrier before readback or blit; uploads SHADER_READ to TRANSFER_DST to SHADER_READ; host writes before each waited submit. Should debug builds also chain VkValidationFeaturesEXT with SYNCHRONIZATION_VALIDATION into the instance create info when the layer is on? The checked-in code would decide it, with no environment variable, and it is cheap to add next to item V.

UiPass::drop calls vkDeviceWaitIdle with no bound (ui.rs:1419), as Core::drop, release_pane and Owner::drop already do. After a fence timeout it waits on the poisoned work until the driver returns DEVICE_LOST (TDR). Accept this as the owner's existing pattern, or ask for it to be named in the lane's not_proven?

F1(b) matches the loader's text, because the count is machine-dependent: 9 per instance here, one per implicit layer the loader drops. Is matching on loader text acceptable, or do you prefer an 'unexpected_loader' counter that must be 0 and is reported apart?

After the rebase, Vulkan mode leaves the receipt's gui.frame.paint (GUI-FRAME-1) at zero, because only CpuChrome fills paint_stats. Should the pass's RecordStats (prims, glyphs, glyph_refusals, missing_resources) fill it in Vulkan mode, or should it be marked null?

The callback is unsafe extern "system" and cannot unwind: it uses atomics and a poison-tolerant Mutex, ignores stderr write errors, and keeps names and text bounded.
